html:
SMTO-SKL-0094 — The Microsoft 365 action was stopped before it finished

GUID: cfb91bca-3007-5aa1-bd8b-af0220a316d0
Slug: microsoft365-operation-cancelled
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • The Microsoft 365 action stopped because the run was cancelled, for example when Stop was selected. If it was sending, saving or uploading something, part of it may already have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the action changed something, like sending mail, editing an event or uploading a file, check Outlook or OneDrive to see whether the change is already there. Cancelling can stop the action after Microsoft has already accepted part or all of it.
  2. If the change is not there, ask the Agent to do it again and let it finish without selecting Stop. Once you know it didn't happen, repeating it won't create a duplicate.
  3. If it was only reading or searching, simply ask the Agent again. Reading doesn't change anything in your Microsoft account, so repeating it is harmless.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reports the action as complete and the result shows up in Outlook or OneDrive.

If it still fails

  • If it stops again without you selecting Stop, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat a send or upload until you've checked it didn't already happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GraphClient.check_cancelled observed the run's cancellation signal (or the socket owner's cancel) before a Graph request, between upload chunks, or while reading a response, and stopped the Microsoft 365 operation.

What this means

  • Graph request/transfer observes the caller or transport owner's cancellation signal. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Graph request/transfer observes the caller or transport owner's cancellation signal.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the last completed request and any already dispatched write.

How to fix it

  • Read the exact resource (Sent Items, the event, contact, or the target drive folder) to see whether the write or any upload chunks took effect before issuing another write. Re-run read-only operations normally; for uploads, start a new upload only after confirming the target file's current state.
  • The read or transfer was cancelled. Inspect any already-started upload before starting another write.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Further work resumes deliberately with earlier effects reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
